definitions.standard: The process of a substance in a liquid state changing to a gaseous state due to an increase in temperature and/or pressure.
definitions.simple: When water slowly turns into air (vapor) even if it's not boiling hot. Like when wet clothes dry on a rope in the sun.
definitions.scientific: The phenomenon of a liquid turning into vapor at any temperature below its boiling point. It is a surface phenomenon and always causes cooling.

linguistics.origin: From Latin 'evaporare', meaning 'to disperse in vapor'.

examples: Water disappearing from a puddle on a sunny day

advanced_data.history: Understood empirically for thousands of years for salt extraction.

common_misconceptions: Evaporation only happens when it is very hot. (It happens at all temperatures, just slower when cold).
Evaporation and boiling are the same. (Boiling happens to the whole liquid, evaporation only at the surface).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Ask the student why they feel cold when they step out of a swimming pool. Explain that the water evaporating from their skin absorbs heat from their body.
